$comment: A small example ruleset for the authoring guide. It rolls 2d6 plus a stat, to show that nothing in the format assumes a d20 or six abilities. Copy it, change the id, and make it yours.
name: Ember Roads

license.attribution: Written for the Marinara Engine docs. Do what you like with it.

coverage.summary: 2d6 plus a stat against a difficulty, a short sheet with Grit and Luck, and one rest.

derived.$comment: What a blow has to beat. Two six-sided dice average seven, so a Guard of six or seven is an even fight.
derived.label: Guard

columns.$comment: A piece of gear with damage dice is something you can swing. The rest of the list is rope and lamp oil, and a fight simply never offers it.
columns.label: Rolls with

lists.$comment: A list with pools: every row is a resource with its own maximum, and the camp rest gives back the ones that recharge there.
lists.label: Limited tricks

gm.checkGuidance: This game uses the Ember Roads rules. When the outcome of a risky action is in doubt, call for a check with one of the skills on the sheet and pick a difficulty from the ladder. The Engine rolls 2d6 and adds the numbers from the sheet. Never write the result yourself.
gm.sheetGuidance: The character sheets below are authoritative. Spend Grit when a character is hurt and Luck when they push a roll, and raise Heat when the party draws attention.

catalogs.$comment: Ready-made knacks the sheet editor offers in a picker. Picked rows are copies the player can edit, and none of this text is ever sent to the model.
catalogs.label: Knacks

entries.label: Road Sense
entries.summary: You read a road the way other people read a face.

values.name: Road Sense
values.notes: Sneak to notice where a road turns bad before you are standing on it.

entries.label: Scrap Whisper
entries.summary: Dead machines tell you what killed them.

values.name: Scrap Whisper
values.notes: Tinker to learn what a broken thing was last used for.

entries.label: Iron Stomach
entries.summary: You can eat what the road offers and keep walking.

values.name: Iron Stomach
values.notes: Ignore the first Shaken you take from bad food or foul water.

entries.$comment: One entry, two rows: the knack itself and the limited use that tracks it.
entries.label: Last Ember
entries.summary: Between camps you can call a friend back from the edge, once for each point of Heart.

values.name: Last Ember
values.notes: Spend 1 Grit to give a downed friend 3 Grit back. Once between camps for each point of Heart.

rows.$comment: The uses follow the character's Heart, so the row stays right as the character grows without anyone editing it. The value is fitted to the column, so a Heart of 3 gives 3 uses and a Heart of 0 or less leaves the trick with none.

entries.label: Coldfire Toss
entries.summary: A jar of blue fire that burns cold and spreads.

values.name: Coldfire Toss
values.notes: Throw a sealed jar. It burns up to three of those you pick, and a friend can be one of them.

entries.label: Hold the Line
entries.summary: You make the people beside you braver than they are.

values.name: Hold the Line
values.notes: Spend 1 Luck to steady one ally who can hear you. In a fight they gain 2 temporary Grit.

mechanics.$comment: This one costs Luck, which the battle block names as the energy pool, so a battle offers it and spends it. Last Ember costs Grit, which is the health pool, and a battle cannot spend hit points as energy: that knack is left out of the fight instead.

battle.$comment: Optional. It does not make battles follow these rules: it lends Marinara's own combat the numbers on the sheet. Grit is what a fight damages, Luck is what a knack spends, there are no slots here, and the knacks a player picked from the catalog become the skills they can use.

combat.$comment: How a fight is resolved by these rules. Nothing here is borrowed from another system: two six-sided dice plus the stat you swing with, against a Guard, with no advantage, no lucky faces, no criticals and one thing to do a turn. The battle block above is what an Engine that cannot read this one falls back to.

layers.$comment: A variant of these rules the player turns on when the game is created. It only narrows and appends: a harsher ladder, a line of guidance for play, a line for world generation, and the knacks that cost Grit left out of the picker.
layers.label: Hard winter
layers.summary: Cold, hunger and short days. Everything is harder and nobody can spare the Grit.

gm.guidance: Hard winter is on. Cold, hunger and short days make everything harder, so use the harsher ladder and let a failed check cost warmth, food or daylight as well as progress.
gm.worldGuidance: Hard winter is on. Build a world locked in a long cold: closed roads, thin stores, and settlements rationing what they have.
